title: Pathway document
description: One pathway's content, instrument, measurement and presentation. Data only: nothing in it is executable (ADR 0003).

translations.description: The Bible translations the pathway quotes, keyed by the abbreviation shown beside each passage, such as 'ESV'. Each one's notice is shown on the credits page.

notice.description: The copyright notice the translation's publisher asks for, word for word.

translation.description: The translation a passage is from when it names none of its own: one of 'translations'.

photos.description: The pathway's photos, keyed by the section each is shown with, such as the hub's next step over a section's photo. Each is a file in the pathways/files folder, with its credit.

file.description: The photo's name in the pathways/files folder, such as 'grass.jpg'.

credit.description: Who the photo is credited to. 'required' when its licence requires a credit, 'courtesy' when its licence does not ask for one, as Unsplash's does not, and 'none' when the author marks it as needing none (public domain, or the author's own). The credits page lists required credits always, courtesy ones while 'show_courtesy_credits' is on, and nothing for 'none'.

text.description: The credit as the credits page lists it, such as 'Photograph by … on Unsplash.'

show_courtesy_credits.description: Whether the credits page lists photos' courtesy credits, those their licence does not ask for. It never hides a credit a licence requires.

scoring.description: How a sort is scored: a named method, frozen once any response is scored with it (ADR 0003).

tie_break.description: When a participant's own sort leaves a framework's leaders too close to call (ticket 30a, ADR 0018). A framework is tied when its leader's unrounded share is at most percent more than another construct's; at most cluster constructs, leader first, enter the tie-break. A participant tied on one framework or both is marked for the tie-break, unless every construct on every framework stands in a band between the lowest and the highest (presentation.standing): then they are flat, and told they are a generalist in presentation.generalist's wording, with nothing asked. With no tie_break, nobody is marked.

percent.description: How much more than another construct's unrounded share, as a percent of it, a leader's may be and still be too close to call with it. 5 when left out.

cluster.description: How many of a tied framework's top constructs, at most, enter the tie-break. 4 when left out.

budget.description: How many 'Which is more true of you?' pairs a participant marked for the tie-break answers, at most (ticket 30b). At least 2, so every tied framework gets a pair when both are tied (ADR 0018). 10 when left out.

statements.description: Three statements for each construct, keyed by its id, that the tie-break's pairs set against each other (ticket 30b). Separate from the instrument's items. Every construct needs them.

link_lifetime_days.description: How many days an observer's link works after it is issued. 30 when left out.

minimum_observers.description: How many observers must have answered before the participant sees any number from their answers. 3 when left out, and never fewer, so no one observer's answers can be picked out.

privacy_notice.description: What an observer is told before any question: who asked, what is stored, what the participant will and will not see, and how to withdraw. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. {name} is replaced with the participant's name. The engine's own draft when left out.

reminder.description: The email that reminds an observer who has not answered, once a week while their link works. It is the first message the observer gets, so it says where their name and email came from, what they are used for, how often and until when. {name} is replaced with the participant's name, {observer} with the observer's, and {until} with the day their link stops working. Each field left out is the engine's draft's.

body.description: Paragraphs are separated by a blank line.

stop.description: The line before the link that stops the reminders.

answer.description: The button that leads to the privacy notice and a fresh link of the observer's own.

details.description: The link beside the button, to the same page, for the privacy notice.

relationship.description: How the observer knows the participant, asked with the observer assessment and stored with it, never used to slice or filter results. Not asked when left out.

question.description: The question's label. {name} is replaced with the participant's name.

persona.description: A short name for the construct shown beside it, such as 'The Philosopher'.

tone.description: The colour of the construct's item scores, from the stylesheet's named tones. Its drawing takes its standing's colour.

results_title.description: The results page's title. {name} is replaced with the participant's name.

generalist.description: What the results page tells a participant whose result, as shown, is flat on both frameworks (measurement.tie_break): that they are a generalist. text for a sort flat on both, which asks no pairs; after_pairs for a result the tie-break's pairs re-weighted that is flat on both, with no framework separated (ADR 0018). Needed whenever the pathway has a tie-break.

tie_break.description: The wording of the tie-break's pair screen (measurement.tie_break, ticket 30b): the question over each pair, the skip, and a quiet label naming each framework, keyed by its id (the framework's own label when left out). Then what the results page says on each framework the answers re-weighted (ticket 30c, ADR 0018): separated, with a new leader (changed) or the same one (same), genuinely balanced, the choices having gone in a circle (circle) or left the best of them level (level), or every pair skipped (skipped), which says nothing about the participant. In those sentences {top} is replaced with the leader after the answers, {previous} with the sort's leader among the tied, {next} with the closest behind the top after the answers, and {names} with the tied constructs as shown, joined "A, B and C", each by its text_label (its label when it has none); no other placeholder is allowed. Needed whenever the pathway has a tie-break.

standing.description: Where a construct's share stands, in words, on the results page and the comparison, by how far it sits from an even share of its framework (an even share is 100 divided among the framework's constructs). A share takes the highest band whose at_least, a percent of an even share, it reaches, in whatever order the bands are written; below them all it takes the below label. The results colour each standing by its band's place, highest first, and the below label in the less-used colour, whatever the labels say. Placeholders (Leading 125, Strong 105, Present 85, Less used) when left out.

comparison.description: What the comparison makes of the self-result beside the observer average, and its wording (ADR 0005). The thresholds are the prototype's when left out.

significant_gap.description: A gap of this many percentage points or more, unrounded, is significant; less is a modest gap. 5 when left out.

agreement.description: How far the observers agree, by the range of their unrounded shares. A range falls in the narrowest band whose up_to it doesn't pass, in whatever order the bands are written; above them all it takes the above label. The prototype's when left out.

seen_by_others.description: Whether others see each construct higher or lower than the participant, beside its drawing, when the gap is significant; otherwise much the same. Placeholders when left out.

gaps.description: The list of the largest gaps: its heading and introduction, each direction's badge and description, and the description of a modest gap. With no gaps wording, the comparison lists no gaps.

prompts.description: The questions to reflect on, shown below the gaps.

sort_wording.description: The sort widget's own wording, around the items and buckets. Each is the engine's own when left out. {name} is replaced with the participant's name, for observers; {count} with the number of items.

send_or_fine_tune.description: Shown to observers only, once every card is placed, beside sending now and fine-tuning first.

send_now_label.description: Shown to observers only, beneath fine-tuning: sending without it. submit_label sends after it.

identifier.description: A stable name, never a position. Starts with a letter.

text.description: One string for every role, or wording per role. A blank observer wording means the same as the participant's.

gap_direction.description: One direction of a gap on the comparison: its badge, and what a significant gap that way may mean.

estimate.description: How long this takes, worded as it is shown, such as 'About 15 minutes'. On a section it shows on the hub and at the top of the section; on a block, just above the block, for a section with several activities.

part_of.description: The section this one is a part of, such as the Strengths assessment within Section 1. A part is listed under that section, has no completion of its own (it is complete once its gate passes), and its pages lead back to that section.

number.description: The section's number as the hub shows it beside the section, such as '01', or '02–04' for a section standing in for three. Without one, the hub shows none.

side_card.description: Draw this section as a card beside the hub's list of sections, below it on a phone, rather than in the list, as Walk with a coach is. The card shows the section's title, this sentence and its status.

wizard.description: Take a participant who has not completed this section to it in place of the hub, shown page by page without the hub's links or the sidebar, beside the section's photo, as Before we begin is. Once complete it is listed in the hub as any other section, unless it is once-only.

once_only.description: Once the participant has completed this section, never show it again: it leaves the hub, the sidebar and the count of sections, and its pages, its answers and its completion lead to the hub, so its answers can be neither seen nor changed, as Before we begin's are in Whatever You Do. Only a wizard may be once-only.

next_step.description: What the hub's next step says while this section is the next step, in place of the section's title and time estimate, such as 'Start with your gifts.' and a sentence on what it asks.

complete_label.description: The wording of the button that completes the section, such as 'Continue →'. Without one, it reads 'Mark complete'.

page_break.description: Where one page of a section ends and the next begins. The page before it ends in 'Continue →'; a section without one is a single page.

variant.description: How the text is set off: plain prose, or a hint box (such as 'The big question').

label.description: An optional short lead-in shown above the body, such as 'The big question'.

body.description: Plain text. A blank line starts a new paragraph.

scripture_reading.description: Passages to read, and a confirmation that opens the activity beneath them.

reference.description: Where the passage is from, such as '1 Corinthians 12:4-11'.

text.description: The passage itself. Plain text; a blank line starts a new paragraph.

translation.description: The translation this passage is from, when not the document's: one of 'translations'.

note.description: What to notice while reading, set beneath the passages.

confirm_label.description: The wording of the confirm control. Defaults to "I have read these".

agreement_scale.description: A prompt the participant rates from 1 to 10, with a label at each end of the scale.

fixed_once_complete.description: Once the rating has been answered and this section completed, it can no longer be changed, even if the section is reopened. For a baseline measured again later.

single_select.description: One choice from a list, such as the reason for taking the course. The answer is the chosen option's identifier.

placeholder.description: What the list shows before anything is chosen, such as 'Select...'. It is never an answer.

id.description: What is stored when this option is chosen. Keep it when rewording the label.

contact_list.description: People who know the participant, a first name and an email address per row, each added with their observer's link or changed on their own. Once its rows are filled, one more is offered. They are kept as contacts, apart from the participant's answers. At most 50.

needed.description: How many of the list's first rows are marked as needed. The section's gate says what completing it takes.

optional.description: How many more rows follow the needed ones, marked as optional.

coach_checklist.description: Choosing a coach: why the choice matters, the candidate's first name, then a question per quality a coach needs, each answered Yes, Not sure or No. The engine's rule turns the answers into going ahead, a second thought or trying someone else. None of the answers is kept.

lead.description: One sentence set off above the body.

body.description: Why the choice matters. A blank line starts a new paragraph.

not_needed.description: The kind of person not to choose, set beside `needed`.

needed.description: The kind of person to choose.

footnote.description: A quieter note beneath, such as why 'coach' and not 'mentor'.

coach_invitation.description: What the coach's link says before the commitments, beneath 'Sam has asked you to be their coach'. {name} is the participant's name. A blank line starts a new paragraph.

coach_accepted.description: What the coach reads once they accept. {name} is the participant's name.

coach_declined.description: What the coach reads once they decline, said as a good outcome. {name} is the participant's name.

questions.description: Asked in order as 'Do you think <name>…', then the question.

id.description: What the answer is sent under. Keep it when rewording the question.

critical.description: A No to a critical question means trying someone else, whatever the other answers.

question.description: Completes 'Do you think <name>…', without a question mark.

why.description: Why the question matters, shown when an answer other than Yes is named.

coach_note.description: The note as the coach reads it (ticket 13).

coach_why.description: Why it matters, as the coach reads it (ticket 13).

coach_brief.description: The guidance for the coach's conversation with the participant about what they are shown. The participant can open it beside the consent to share it, and a coach who has accepted sees it on their link. Nothing is sent.

title.description: Which conversation this is, such as 'Session 1 – Their gifts'.

length.description: How long the conversation might take, such as '45–60 minutes'.

questions.description: Questions for the coach to ask, in order.

watch_for.description: What the coach should look out for, in order.

avoid.description: The one thing the coach should not do.

sort_assessment.description: The instrument's sort: every item placed in a bucket and fine-tuned, then scored once as a result.

coach_brief.description: The guidance for the coach's conversation about these results and their comparison, which the coach sees once the participant shares them (ticket 25a).

section_link.description: A way to another section, shown with that section's title and the participant's status there.

body.description: Plain text saying what is there. A blank line starts a new paragraph.

button_label.description: The wording of a button that leads there, such as 'Open Strengths Assessment →'. Without one, the section's title is the link.

finished.description: What the link says once the linked section is complete, in place of its body and button label, such as 'View my results →'. Its button then leads to the results of the sort in that section, if it holds one, and otherwise to the section.

holds_what_follows.description: Hold the rest of this section shut until the linked section's gate passes, as a scripture reading does until it is confirmed.

sort_results.description: A sort's results, shown in full as its results page shows them, once the participant has them; before then, nothing.

sort.description: The identifier of the sort whose results these are.

comparison_link.description: A card for the way to a sort's comparison with the participant's observers, once there is a result: its title, where it stands (waiting for answers, ready to view, or viewed) and the results page's 'Compare with how others see you →', which warns before answer collection freezes as that one does.

sort.description: The identifier of the sort whose comparison this leads to.

title.description: The card's title, such as 'How others see you'.

download.description: A file for the participant to download, such as a workbook to print. The app serves it only to a participant who has reached this block.

file.description: The PDF's name in the pathways/files folder, such as 'whatever-you-do-workbook-section-2.pdf'.

body.description: Plain text saying what the file is for. A blank line starts a new paragraph.

button_label.description: The wording of the button that downloads it, such as 'Download Section 2 (PDF)'.

placeholder.description: Ghost text in the empty box, such as 'Dear me,'. A hint only: it is never saved as the answer.

gate.description: What must be true before the participant may complete this section. Every clause must pass.

clause.description: One requirement, chosen from a fixed set and configured. Never an expression (ADR 0003).

clause_message.description: Shown to the participant when this clause, and no other, is what is still missing.

has_answer.description: The block has been answered. Blank text and an empty list do not count as an answer.

min_text_length.description: The block's text answer is at least this long, not counting space at either end.

entry_count.description: The block holds at least this many entries.

only_with_content.description: Count only entries with something in them, so blank rows a widget seeded do not count.

allow_none.description: Also pass with no entries at all, for a list the participant may leave for later.

distinct_value_count.description: The block's entries hold at least this many different values for one field.

every_entry_has.description: Every entry holds a value for this field. True of no entries at all, so pair it with entry_count.

comparison_visited.description: The participant has gone from this sort's results to its comparison with their observers, whatever it shows: below the minimum of observers, its explanation counts.

links_issued.description: At least this many of the people a contact list or coach checklist holds have a working link. Issued is enough: nobody need have answered.

seed.description: Where this bucket's sliders start, and so the answer an untouched slider gives: a whole number, as every answer value is.

loads.description: The constructs this item loads onto: exactly one in each framework.

label.description: The construct's name beside its drawing: on the results page, the comparison and a coach's view of the results.

text_label.description: The construct's name wherever text names it, such as the tie-break's sentences, the comparison's largest gaps and the heading over its item scores, when it is written otherwise than beside its drawing (Whatever You Do's "deacon" is "Deacon" in text). The label when left out.
